title: Scorecard weights
decision: Propensity score = {w_usage} usage growth + {w_builders} new builders + {w_eng} engagement + {w_breadth} product breadth, each bucketed to 0–100.
why: Recent momentum is the strongest sign of near-term growth; more people building today usually means more workloads in production soon. Commit pressure is a risk, not growth, so it's an alert instead.
possibly: Possibly we can test the weights against real history, then move to a machine learning model that keeps top reasons.

title: Signal windows
decision: Usage growth over {win_usage} months; new builders over {win_builders} days; meetings and calls over {win_eng} days.
why: Long enough to smooth out noise, short enough to reflect what the customer is doing now.
possibly: Possibly we can count new builders only if they deployed something, and exclude automated accounts.

title: Pool of funds formula
decision: Pool of funds = unused commit + open pipeline; opportunity value = propensity score ÷ 100 × pool of funds.
why: Unused commit is the most urgent money; pipeline is included because SA and FDE help often decides whether those deals close. Opportunity value is for ranking, not a forecast.
possibly: Possibly we can weight pipeline by deal stage and divide opportunity value by the SA/FDE hours an account needs.

title: Alert thresholds
decision: Commit at risk below {car_pace} On-track %; Renewal coming within {renewal_days} days; Builder surge {surge_min}+ in {win_builders} days; Usage spike +{spike_min} in a month; Usage drop −{drop_max} over 3 months; New product in {win_newprod} days.
why: Scores say who; alerts say when. Six alerts is enough, and each one has an owner and an action.
possibly: Possibly we can tune thresholds by checking which alerts led to real growth.

title: On-track bands
decision: On track at {on_track_good}+, Slightly behind at {on_track_warn}–89%, Behind below {on_track_warn}.
why: Simple bands for readability; the Behind line matches the Commit at risk alert. On-track % assumes even spending, which overstates risk for seasonal businesses like retail.
possibly: Possibly we can adjust On-track % for seasonality using spending curves from similar accounts.

title: Type-of-help cut-offs
decision: Propensity score {score_high}+ and pool of funds {pool_high}+.
why: Two simple questions are easy to explain and easy to challenge; the cut-offs put roughly the right number of accounts in each type for the team's size.
possibly: Possibly we can set cut-offs from data and use different cut-offs by segment.

title: Team capacity
decision: {sas} SAs × {sa_load} accounts = {sa_slots} SA slots; {fdes} FDEs × {fde_load} deep engagements = {fde_slots} FDE slots.
why: Without a capacity limit, a priority list is a wish list. A visible cut-off line makes the trade-off clear.
possibly: Possibly we can use real SA and FDE hours from the engagement tracker and plan capacity by region.

title: Comparison group
decision: {holdout_share} of accounts that qualify for scaled help are chosen at random for the comparison group.
why: Accounts with high scores often grow anyway; random selection makes the two groups alike, so the difference is fair.
possibly: Possibly we can rotate the comparison group each quarter so no customer is left out for long.
